newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki seen off with Wall St, but bears at bay.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki seen off with Wall St, but bears at bay.

text.p: Shares were seen opening lower on Wednesday after the Dow industrials and Nokia's ADR fell overnight, but brokers said they did not expect any big drop.
"We'll open down slightly because Nokia was off in New York, but I don't expect anything radical," one broker said.
On Wall Street, Nokia fell $0-3/8 to $64-1/2 (329.00 markka) after closing at 332.50 markka in Helsinki.

Another broker predicted the HEX would fall by less than half a percentage point at the open, but said that the market could find the ingredients for a turnaround during the day because sentiment had not been spoiled.
The bourse could be helped by a 1.4 percent rise in U.S. paper industry stocks overnight, brokers said.
UPM-Kymmene could move into focus ahead of its first quarter earnings report on Thursday, they said.
With interest rate jitters resurfacing in the U.S., eyes would be on U.S. economic indicators this week, including PPI due at 1530/1230 GMT today and CPI tomorrow, brokers said.
"But we had a lively day of trade yesterday, despite the U.S. figures," one broker said, suggesting that activity would not necessarily dry up today.
